key_insight: Near the dilation boundary, diamond-norm tomography loses Heisenberg scaling abruptly, while Choi trace-norm tomography transitions gradually to classical scaling.
engineering_relevance: These bounds guide quantum-channel characterization budgets by linking required black-box queries to channel dimensions, Kraus rank, accuracy, and error metric.
method: Parameterize channels by dilation rate τ = r d₂/d₁ and resolve the near-boundary regime τ > 1.
Prove a diamond-norm query lower bound Ω(r d₁ d₂/ε²), matching known upper bounds.
Establish Choi trace-norm complexity Θ(d₁²/ε + min{(τ−1)d₁², (τ−1)²d₁²d₂²}/ε²).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports matching theoretical query-complexity bounds, not experimental or hardware evaluations.
watch_item: Optimal black-box query counts do not by themselves establish practical runtime, measurement overhead, or robustness to hardware noise.
paper_title: Quantum channel tomography: optimal bounds in the near-boundary regime
